report.program: School-based counseling, mentoring, family support and youth opportunity programs

acceptance.evidence: Independent conditional-alpha source/model audit: outputs/chicago-youth-guidance-audit/audit.md. Donor HOLD retained; root integration pending.

report.priceScope: Conditional whole-recipient scenario; Chicago WOW mental health quantified, other net health unknown

what: Youth Guidance provides school-based counseling and mentoring alongside family, afterschool and career support.
Its WOW program serves girls and young women, including students across Chicagoland and Waukegan.
An unrestricted gift supports the full national organization and its broader portfolio.
strengths: A Chicago randomized WOW study measured mental-health outcomes against usual services.
Original audited accounts establish full-recipient costs across three consecutive years.
Current annual reporting separates local WOW reach from national delivery.
reservations: Trial utilities and duration are modeled, and current delivery may differ from the research setting.
No costed unfunded gift tranche or measured unrestricted funding response is established.
Other program health, partner resources and exact metro residence remain incompletely quantified.

sections.what: This is an ordinary unrestricted-gift assessment of Youth Guidance, EIN 36-2167032. It includes BAM, WOW, school counseling, STRIVE, afterschool, family support, career services and EVOLVE across all regions. Chicago’s page establishes actual services, beyond a headquarters address. [Scope](https://youth-guidance.org/locations/youth-guidance-chicago/) [Giving](https://youth-guidance.org/get-involved/donate/) Only health accruing to residents of the Chicago-Naperville-Elgin MSA is credited to this edition.
sections.monitoring: FY25’s report lists 4,331 WOW participants nationally and 3,649 across Chicagoland/Waukegan. Those are reach counts, not completed courses or counterfactual health gains. A newer brochure instead says more than 4,600 in 2025; the model consistently uses the annual report. [Report, pp. 6 and 16](https://youth-guidance.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Youth-Guidance-FY25-Annual-Report.pdf) [Brochure](https://youth-guidance.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/program-onepagers/YG_National_WOW_One-Pager_v2026.pdf) Request deduplicated participant-year counts, residence, age, dosage, entry symptoms, survey response and repeated participation. Current before/after symptom percentages cannot substitute for controlled effects.
sections.qualitative: WOW has unusually direct local causal evidence: a randomized Chicago high-school study with 3,749 assigned students measured PTSD, anxiety and depression symptoms. Its economic analysis maps survey scores to utility, takes the lower utility for co-occurring depression/PTSD and posits effect duration. These are not observed clinical diagnoses or directly measured QALYs. [Trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10246898/) The current brochure describes college-educated counselors and grades 6–12, while the evaluated service used master-level counselors with high-school students; equivalence needs checking. [Current delivery](https://youth-guidance.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/program-onepagers/YG_National_WOW_One-Pager_v2026.pdf) BAM adds a plausible safety pathway, but later trials had less consistent results and pooled economic returns include non-health benefits. Arrests, graduation and earnings are not automatically health gains. [Four studies](https://crimelab.uchicago.edu/projects/becoming-a-man-bam/)
sections.cost:
The illustrative central scenario is approximately $31.94 million per 10 Chicago-MSA QALYs, not a measured gift return or a scalable purchase quote. Full-recipient gross recognized expense C=$54,857,607 remains in the numerator. Only WOW’s mental-health channel is quantified, while all other signed net health is conditionally zero. The unknown other portfolio could improve or reverse the result.

Q_MSA=b*(L*g*q*t*D+Hlocal). Central: L=3,649 local annual reach; g=.95 residence share; q=2300/58025=.039638 participant-equivalent utility gain reconstructed from the trial’s own economic analysis; t=.5 current-delivery transfer; D=.5 years; b=.5 funding response; Hlocal=0. This produces 17.1759 conditional MSA QALYs. The original program ICER is used only to recover its utility-model coefficient; this report replaces its cost boundary with the whole organization and does not import its program price. [Trial economic methods/Table 5](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10246898/)

q is already participant-equivalent; multiplying it by the 65% invitation take-up again would double-discount. No separate full-course completion claim is made. The current-dose discount is inside t. No suicide, lifetime protection, anxiety add-on, victim injury or wage-to-QALY conversion is credited. The one-year scenario gives $15.97m; the favorable joint case $3.79m and poor case $758.54m per 10 QALYs. These are stress cases, not confidence intervals. Zero funding response or effect gives no finite positive price; negative other-program net health can reverse the sign. All parameters and 15 cases are inspectable below.

The recovered q coefficient is approximate because the study's cost and ICER are rounded; it is a participant-equivalent economic-model coefficient, not a newly estimated IV effect. The paper's prose and table disagree on threshold benefit days, so no threshold-day assertion is imported.
sections.funding:
Audited operating expenses were $46,884,765 (FY23), $56,011,499 (FY24) and $54,652,685 (FY25), before direct event benefits netted against revenues. The FY25 model adds $204,922 of those benefits. Cash was $1,281,080; general-expenditure financial assets $5,273,375; drawn credit $800,000. These are historical balances, not a current funding gap. [FY24 audit](https://youth-guidance.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/FS_2024-Youth-Guidance-Final.pdf) [FY25 audit, pp. 4–6, 14](https://youth-guidance.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/FS_2025-Youth-Guidance-Final.pdf)

The $80m Bright Futures campaign combines an impact fund and endowment; it does not demonstrate that the next unrestricted dollar expands Chicago WOW. [Campaign](https://youth-guidance.org/get-involved/bright-futures/) The city vendor list shows newer contracts, so a historic proposed-cut story cannot establish today's loss of funding. [Contracts](https://webapps1.chicago.gov/vcsearch/city/vendors/99253665A/contracts) Donor recommendation: HOLD. Request current accounts, restrictions, grant renewal/reimbursement status, staffing capacity and a priced incremental plan. The official page provides a route and recipient EIN; no transaction or restricted-gift terms were verified.

The audit's Davee BAM/WOW funds are purpose restricted rather than legally perpetual, with distributions subject to a 4% spending policy. This is not unrestricted cash immediately available to cover a donor's preferred program. A current board/funder-approved spending plan is needed.

model.costScope: Full Youth Guidance national audited FY25 expenses plus direct special-event benefits; recognized resources included. K adds unknown unrecognized resources. No restriction to WOW or Chicago costs.
model.geographicAttribution: Only local WOW reach L=3649 times g=.95 judgment, not national N=4331 times a headquarters share. Chicago and Waukegan anchors intersect the 13-county MSA; exact residence pending.
model.formula: Q_all=b*(N*q*t*D+H); Q_MSA=b*(L*g*q*t*D+Hlocal); cost=C+K; price per 10 QALYs=10*cost/Q_MSA only when Q_MSA>0.
model.counterfactual: Original trial: usual school/community electives and services. Current scenario discounts transfer and allows zero resource response if a gift replaces grants/reserves; no assumption that participants otherwise receive nothing.
model.attribution: Whole-recipient ordinary gift; national costs retained; only MSA health counted. Other portfolio treated as unknown signed health, not asserted valueless. q preserves economic-study participant denominator.
model.uncertainty: Utility mapping, effect persistence, current counselor/age/dose comparability, survey response, duplicate reach, finance elasticity, residence and other portfolio can dominate. Scenarios are not confidence intervals.
model.nativeOutcomes: WOW randomized symptom scales and mapped combined depression/PTSD utility; annual reach; recipient audited expenses. BAM arrests/education not converted to health.

inputs.name: C
inputs.unit: USD FY2025 gross recognized whole-recipient expenses
inputs.rationale: Audited expenses $54,652,685 plus $204,922 direct event benefits netted against revenue. All programs, regions, administration and fundraising retained. Includes recorded donated services and in-kind resources; not cash marginal cost.

inputs.name: N
inputs.rationale: Annual report page 6; differs from 2026 brochure's more-than-4600 2025 claim. Use report consistently, no blending.

inputs.name: L
inputs.rationale: Annual report page 16. Not verified unique completed trial-equivalent courses or exact MSA resident count.

inputs.name: q
inputs.unit: trial-model utility gain per participant-equivalent year
inputs.rationale: Reconstruct 2300/58025=0.039638 from original Table 5's combined depression/PTSD ICER and cost per actual participant. Study assigns minimum condition utility to avoid additive comorbidity. Algebra recovers the economic model's participant-equivalent mapped gain, not directly observed health utility or a local gift price. Transfer remains judgment.

inputs.name: t
inputs.unit: current effective-dose and population transfer multiplier
inputs.rationale: Discount for grades 6–12 vs original high-school sample, intensity/completion, staff qualifications, survey mapping and current counterfactual. Does not reapply the trial's 65% offer take-up; q already uses a participant-equivalent denominator.

inputs.name: D
inputs.unit: years of utility benefit per annual participant reach
inputs.rationale: Half-year benefit then zero. No lifetime protection or two-year accumulation; same participant across fiscal years must not receive duplicate long-term benefit.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Hypothetical half response relative to historic service mix. Reserves, restrictions, contracted revenue and staffing can make this zero. No verified incremental tranche.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: MSA residence share of local-reach benefits
inputs.rationale: Chicago and Waukegan are local anchors; Chicagoland is not a precise 13-county residence boundary. This is not 95% of national output.

inputs.name: K
inputs.unit: USD unrecognized net partner resource costs
inputs.rationale: Conditionally zero, stress-tested at 25% of C; school space/staff and unpaid resources not priced. Recorded donated resources are not added twice.

inputs.name: H
inputs.unit: signed annual non-WOW national QALYs before funding response
inputs.rationale: Conditionally zero. BAM and other work can benefit or harm; arrest reductions and earnings cannot be directly relabeled QALYs.

inputs.name: Hlocal
inputs.unit: signed annual other-portfolio MSA QALYs before funding response
inputs.rationale: Conditionally zero, separate from national health; ±50 cases are judgments with overlap deducted in future work.

sensitivity: Fifteen cases include zero finance, zero clinical effect, negative other-portfolio health, alternative utility channels, shorter/longer duration, lower reach/residence and extra resources.
Favorable and poor joint cases are judgments, not statistical bounds or accepted EV ranks.
Current brochure/annual-report reach mismatch and clinical-delivery changes require clarification before beta.
missingInputs: Current signed grant ledger, unrestricted marginal funding plan and capacity/finance response.
Deduplicated adequate-dose participant years and exact MSA residence, including repeated participants.
Direct local utility follow-up, clinical qualification fidelity and persistence beyond survey measurement.
Signed BAM and other portfolio net health with overlap excluded, plus unrecognized school/partner resources.
